reviews.title: Great budget gaming board- my first Asrock build
reviews.comment: The B760 Pro RS by Asrock About a hundred bucks new at the time of this review. Let's get the cons out of the way first: You cannot set up Raid 0 on PCI Express ssd drives. This was my fault not researching more before buying so I did not take off any stars. Okay, that was the single 'con' of this board. This is an unbelievably well built mobo- I included pictures. Yes, that is a micro ATX case, pretty much generic, small, and.. uh, small. And those GPU's are the RTX 3090ti FE, and the Red Devil Ultimate RX 6900 XT, both are huge, heavy GPU's. Both required a bunch of struggling to fit into that case, especially the RX 6900 XT, there isn't even a millimeter of clearance. I was prying, pushing, flexing the mobo way more than anyone with any decent sense would, I truly thought theres no way this will post when I turn it on. But it did, and I am impressed, I've never given a motherboard a beating like this. My last 5 or 6 builds have been exclusively ROG Maximus Hero's, along with one Maximus extreme... the last one before this was a Z690 hero that I paid about $600 for when they first came out. That passmark score is from this Asrock board, but you'd never know, judging by the performance... looks just like the Republic of Gamers  scores.. In other words, I will definitely be trying Asrock for some builds going forward. This was a great experience.
reviews.author: michael berring
